definitions.gloss: decolorizing agent; bleach used to remove color
definitions.explanation: A chemical product that removes color from hair, fabric, or other material. Especially common for the hair bleach used to lighten hair before dyeing.

examples.japanese: {脱色剤|だっしょくざい}を{使|つか}う。
{髪|かみ}を{染|そ}める{前|まえ}に{脱色剤|だっしょくざい}で{明|あか}るくする。
examples.english: Before dyeing the hair, you lighten it with a decolorizing agent.

examples.japanese: {脱色剤|だっしょくざい}は{刺激|しげき}が{強|つよ}いので、{使|つか}いすぎに{注意|ちゅうい}する。
examples.english: Decolorizing agents are harsh, so be careful not to overuse them.

notes:
Compound of {脱色|だっしょく} (removing color) + {剤|ざい} (agent, preparation). Most often refers to hair bleach, but also to color removers for cloth or other materials.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {脱色剤|だっしょくざい}を{塗|ぬ}る: to apply the decolorizing agent
- {市販|しはん}の{脱色剤|だっしょくざい}: a commercially sold bleach

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {漂白剤|ひょうはくざい}: bleach — mainly for whitening laundry and removing stains
- {染料|せんりょう}: dye — adds color rather than removing it
